label: The count
closed_by: story-site, seeded on 27 October from the newsroom's records (state.json v0 to v3, sources.json by published date, the timeline, the compromise and impact ledgers, BREAKING-001); from Day 7 on, the desk

headline._: NIST rates it 9.8; sites come back online; one claimed break-in is withdrawn.
headline.exec: One claimed break-in was withdrawn. Still no organisation says it was hit. 50 of 51 sites that went dark are back.
headline.security: NVD: CVSS 3.1 9.8. 735 public repositories. Vendors: 10 of their products vulnerable, 26 not, 16 still being checked.
headline.engineer: The inventory grows to 751 products; 389 not yet assessed. Check bought-in software, not only your own servers.
headline.journalist: Sophos withdraws its claimed compromise: don't report a confirmed break-in. 3 candidate incidents, none linked yet.
headline.general: Most websites that went offline are back. Nothing has been taken from people that anyone knows of.

items.text: Sites taken offline: 10 reported becomes 51 listed, 50 back online, 1 still dark.
Three incidents are named as possibly linked (Czech university, two Japanese firms); none confirmed.
NIST scores both flaws CVSS 3.1 9.8, beside the CNA's 9.2.
The Dutch inventory: 109 of 751 products known affected.
Sophos withdraws its claim of a successful compromise.
Switzerland: just over 23,000 of nearly 690,000 servers still affected a day after the fix.
